chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the time of al-Maghrib.
So he said: “If it is gentler for you and more feasible for you in your salat, and you are occupied with your needs, then you have until a quarter of the night.”
He said: Then he said to me: “And that is for one who is present in his town.”

key_terms.أَرْفَقَ: more gentle and easier for the person
key_terms.بَلَدِهِ: his town or place of residence
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the time of the Maghrib prayer

ai.seo_question: Until when may Maghrib prayer be delayed according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time of Maghrib prayer and indicates an allowance to delay it until a quarter of the night when that is easier and more manageable for the person, especially when occupied with personal needs. It reflects a jurisprudential ruling concerning the timing of salat and the practical flexibility recognized in worship.
